+# Review gates: close the agent-text and waiver bypasses (audit P0)
+
+Status: draft
+Source: docs/analysis/review-process-audit-2026-11-12.md, sections "Критичные находки" 1-4 (origin: agent-finding)
+
+## Problem
+
+On hosts without operator cards (Claude Code, Codex, other AGENTS.md hosts) an agent can close or publish a managed review round without a human, because several completion gates accept text the agent itself writes.
+
+- The verifier gate passes when `report.md` contains `Not verified: N` (`src/review/readiness.ts:228-235`). The refusal message tells the agent which line to add.
+- The moved-head gate passes when the report's first line names a SHA and says the PR moved (`src/review/complete-head-gate.ts:56-58`).
+- `review complete --head <sha>` replaces the reviewed head recorded at `review start` with only a warning (`src/review/managed.ts:1043-1055`), which makes the moved-head check false.
+- A waiver of any one of `files-covered`, `blast-radius`, `reviewers`, `ledger` empties the whole research-error list (`src/review/managed.ts:1105-1107`).
+- `publishReview` never reads `manifest.status`, takes no completion lock and skips the round-record tamper check and the evidence-level check that exist only on the `complete` path (`src/review/publish.ts:146-180`).
+- The orchestrator skill tells keryx shell to pass `model_tier` on reviewer dispatches; `spawn_subagent` ignores that field (`src/harness/tool/builtin/spawn-subagent-tool.ts:1497-1498`). The accepted field is `model_class`, which no review skill names.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+A managed round cannot be closed or published on the strength of agent-written text alone, a waiver lifts only the item it names, publish and complete evaluate the same gates, and reviewer dispatches on keryx shell carry a model field the spawn tool honours.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Источник: docs/analysis/review-process-audit-2026-11-12.md
+- Эффект (формализация агента): no completion or publish gate of a managed review can be satisfied by text the reviewing agent wrote without an operator card or a TTY, a readiness waiver removes only the errors of the waived item, and the reviewer model class chosen by `keryx review tier` is the one the keryx shell child actually runs on.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): the new regression tests named in the acceptance criteria fail on `66ee00117` and pass on the flow's head; `keryx review complete` on a fixture package with unverified majors and a `Not verified: N` line in `report.md` is refused when no operator proof is present.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Verifying host-question answers cryptographically (`completion-host.ts`); this flow only marks them as unverified in the published body.
+- Locking `ingest` and `ledger build`, and widening the completion snapshot (flow 490).
+- Any change to which reviewers run or how findings are scored (flow 489).

The refusal names both SHAs. The manifest records `head_override: { from, to, operator_quote, time, confirmedVia? }`.

+# Review signal and cost: usage capture, one severity rubric, bounded report, seeded benchmark (audit P1)
+
+Status: draft
+Source: docs/analysis/review-process-audit-2026-11-12.md, sections "Критичные находки" 5-6, "Функциональность", "Продукт" (origin: agent-finding)
+
+## Problem
+
+Nobody can say what a review round costs, how long it takes, or how precise it is, and the report buries its verdict.
+
+- Token usage reads `known=0` in every modern package and wall-clock time is recorded nowhere, while a round dispatches 22-26 agents (audit run-history numbers, not recomputed).
+- 79% of 739 retained findings are `minor` or `info`; the verifier refutes about 2% and the premise judge upholds 95%. Only 17 findings carry a disposition, so precision cannot be read, and no seeded-bug benchmark exists for the core reviewers.
+- The canonical rubric says `blocker` is exactly four shapes, yet `review-highload` rates checklist items `blocker` 11 times and `review-backend` 7 times; `review-frontend` and `review-logic` do the same.
+- The orchestrator teaches `class_scope.sites: []` for negative enumeration (`SKILL.md:1361`) while `reviewer-finding.schema.json:158` requires `minItems: 1`.
+- Reviewer skills carry inline markdown finding templates (`Why it matters` / `Fix`) that omit the `evidence` and `confidence` fields the schema requires.
+- `report.md` embeds the whole findings JSON after the readable part (23k words for PR 1124).
+- "Cross-family review" records an intention; `keryx providers cross-family` never dispatches a reviewer (`src/standard/command-registry.ts:1742-1743`).
+- `stack_requires` dispatches a reviewer when any listed tag is present (`SKILL.md:861`), so a React project without MobX gets the MobX lane.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+Every closed round states its measured cost and duration, reviewers apply one severity rubric and one finding contract, the published report leads with the verdict and stays short, and a seeded benchmark gives a precision and recall number for the core reviewers that CI reproduces.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Источник: docs/analysis/review-process-audit-2026-11-12.md
+- Эффект (формализация агента): a closed review package records tokens and wall-clock per dispatch and prints them in the report; no bundled reviewer skill assigns a severity outside the canonical rubric; the skill text and the finding schema agree; the report body is bounded; a benchmark over seeded defects reports precision and recall for the core reviewer set.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): run one managed round on a real PR after the flow lands and read the first lines of `report.md` (time, tokens, verdict); run the benchmark command and compare its numbers with the committed baseline.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Changing which reviewers `keryx review required` selects, beyond the `stack_requires` semantics.
+- A round state machine and module restructuring (flow 490).
+- CLI help, glossary and guide (flow 491).

+# Review architecture: round state machine in code, byte ceiling for skills, staged modules, one host port (audit P2)
+
+Status: draft
+Source: docs/analysis/review-process-audit-2026-11-12.md, section "Архитектура" and "Харнесы" (origin: agent-finding)
+
+## Problem
+
+A review round has no state model in code. The order of steps lives in 233 KB of orchestrator prose (`SKILL.md` 147 KB, `SKILL.detail.md` 86 KB), and the code is 58 independent subcommands that each re-derive state from package files. Every new failure is therefore answered with a new paragraph and a new gate: 93 commits to the orchestrator skill in 60 days.
+
+- Rules exist twice. `classifyRoundNeed` (`src/review/round-need.ts:102`) has no caller outside tests; the agent executes the same rule from prose (`SKILL.md:29`).
+- The skill length ceiling counts lines and only moves down (`src/gdskills/skill-length-ceilings.ts`). The orchestrator sits exactly at 1571 lines and grows inside lines: the longest is 5023 characters (`SKILL.md:128`). `SKILL.detail.md` has no ceiling.
+- The lifecycle enum has five statuses; only `draft` and `closed` are written.
+- `src/commands/review.ts` is 5940 lines; `src/review/managed.ts` is 3187 lines; `src/review` holds 161 non-test modules in one directory. Eight `jev-*-config.ts` files are the same reader with a different key.
+- Four unrelated abstractions share the word "host": `host-profile.ts`, `completion-host.ts`, the hierarchical `review/agents` engine and the flat path's package files.
+- `ingest` and `ledger build` write `findings.json` and `research.json` without the completion lock; the completion snapshot omits files that readiness reads.
+- No test runs start, slice, ledger, ingest, complete and publish end to end on a ledger that `ledger build` produced.
+- Codex, opencode and Grok are routed to the autonomous runner on keryx's own provider; opencode and Grok are not in `REVIEW_HOSTS`.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+The round's next step is computed by keryx, not read from prose; the orchestrator skill shrinks to executing what the command returns; skills are bounded by bytes; the review code is grouped by stage; one host port describes what each harness can do.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Источник: docs/analysis/review-process-audit-2026-11-12.md
+- Эффект (формализация агента): an agent on any host drives a round by repeatedly asking keryx for the next step and its inputs; rules such as "is a round needed" are evaluated by a command; the orchestrator skill is materially smaller; adding a host or a gate touches one declared place.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): the byte size of `review-orchestrator/SKILL.md` plus `SKILL.detail.md` before and after; an end-to-end test that completes a fixture round using only the step command; the number of files touched to add a host value.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Behaviour changes to gates (flow 488) and to scoring or reports (flow 489).
+- New reviewers or new harness adapters for opencode and Grok beyond naming them in the capability matrix.
+- This flow is large. It is expected to be split into phases after `flow plan`; the criteria below describe the end state.

 It prints the decision and the reason, and reuses the previous record when

 ## Readiness — the checklist behind `completed` and behind publishing
 
 `keryx review readiness <review-id-or-path> [--json]` reads the package and prints every readiness item, READY or NOT READY, each with the evidence and the command that repairs it. It writes nothing, and exits non-zero when the verdict is NOT READY. Only item 9 reaches GitHub (the PR's own file list); the TUI and `review status` read the package alone.
 
 1. `files-covered` — every changed file is in a wave or carries a recorded waiver.
 2. `blast-radius` — no file the blast radius cut is left unreviewed. A cut radius writes `chunks.json`; run `keryx review chunks plan`, `estimate`, `next`/`record`, `merge`. Then bring in what the passes found: `merge` lists the findings and how many `findings.json` lacks; `keryx review ingest --review-id <id>` records them as `review-regression/<chunk>`; ingest and the report are repeated when a pass finished after the report was written. `review complete` warns about a pass finding still out of `findings.json` and does not refuse. In an unattended run every wave runs without a question, up to the 25-pass ceiling; in an interactive run the operator is asked once: in keryx shell call `review_chunks_answer` (a card, never a terminal); elsewhere the operator runs `keryx review chunks estimate --package <dir> --answer yes --quote "<their words>"` in their terminal; unattended, record Not run.
 3. `reviewers` — every planned reviewer was dispatched and its result ingested.
-4. `verifier` — the verifier checked every finding it should, or the report says how many it did not.
+4. `verifier` — the verifier checked every blocker/major finding, or the operator waived the item; a `Not verified: N` line in the report no longer passes it.
 5. `ledger` — the ledger is READY.
 6. `coverage-md` — coverage.md does not list a reviewer as `run` that the dispatch record says did not finish. Re-run `keryx review ingest` for the package.
 7. `head` — the report's head is the PR head.
 8. `report-names` — pending mutation candidates and parity warnings are named in the report.
 9. `pr-files` — the changed-file count equals the PR's own file list. A recount more than 3x the recorded scope is refused: it came from the wrong base. Recount with `keryx review blast-radius --package <ref> --changed <the PR's files>`.

Re-quote one distinct line and re-ingest, record a disposition, or the operator waives the item.

The text reaches the reviewer in slices small enough to finish.
 
 0. **Publish the plan before anything else (keryx shell).** Your first tool call is `plan_set` with `step-0`…`step-14` and `step-10b` all `pending`. A shell turn that has open plan items is continued by the host; a turn that ends on a text reply is over, and a message saying the review "cannot be honestly completed" ends the run with nothing reviewed. Never end the turn while a step is `pending` or `in_progress`: mark it `blocked` only with a cause you cannot fix with a command, and otherwise keep working. Step 6a then updates this plan rather than creating it.
 1. **Slice first.** `keryx review slice --ref <base> --package <package> --host <host>` after `keryx review start`. It writes `<package>/slices/slice-NN.diff` files of at most 150000 bytes each and a `manifest.json` carrying a wave budget (`--wave-bytes`, never below the slice ceiling; default by `--host`: 60000 on keryx-shell, 150000 elsewhere): what ONE reviewer dispatch may total, so a role owning many slices is dispatched in slice waves that each fit the child deadline. On keryx shell with a large diff pass a small `--max-bytes` (for example 18000) and `--wave-bytes` (for example 54000) so no wave outruns a reviewer's five minutes; ledgers (csv, lockfiles, snapshots, generated files) are listed under `omissions` with a reason — list them in the report as not reviewed, never as clean.
 2. **Slices travel by path; on keryx shell, only by `context_files`.** The slices sit under the project (`<package>/slices`). On keryx shell pass each reviewer its slice paths in `spawn_subagent`'s `context_files`: the host copies the text into that reviewer's task, so you never paste or retype a slice. Elsewhere name the slice paths in the prompt. Put the `slices` ids in its reviewer-input. A dispatch that names a git range but no slice leaves the reviewer with nothing to read — that is `BLOCKED`, not a review.
 3. **Check before dispatch, every payload.** `keryx review dispatch-check --payload <file> --manifest <package>/slices/manifest.json --package <package>` for the wave; exit 1 means a payload names no slice, is over the wave ceiling (dispatch fewer slices, then the next wave), names a `skill_path` or `context_doc` that does not exist (`REVIEWER_INPUT_PATH_MISSING`), belongs to an unconfirmed over-threshold plan (`REVIEWER_INPUT_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED`), or breaks `reviewer-input.schema.json`. Fix it; do not dispatch around it.
 4. **One batch.** Dispatch the whole wave — up to 10 reviewers — in one message, not one at a time. On keryx shell every round reviewer's `spawn_subagent` carries `review_wave: {"package": "<package>", "pass": "round"}` (a wave outside it counts against the turn's 32 children) and a `timeout_ms` that fits its wave: the default 300000 is sized for a wave of 60000 bytes, so a larger `--wave-bytes` needs a larger `timeout_ms`. Give each reviewer `max_rounds` of at least 40 (the default); a reviewer that spends its rounds reading the skill and the schema returns nothing. **Incomplete means the next wave while it makes progress, Not run when it stalls.** Every reviewer result lists the `slices` it covered, in its `REVIEW_RESULT` object, as ids (`"slices": ["slice-01", "slice-02"]`); an object with an `id` and an optional `coverage` note (`{"id": "slice-01", "coverage": "read in full"}`) is read the same way. An object with a `status` counts only when it is DONE, COMPLETE, COVERED or OK (any case); a slice marked NOT_READ, INCOMPLETE, SKIPPED or PARTIAL is not covered, so give a slice you did not read no `status` of that kind and leave it out. An entry with no id counts for nothing. **One driver file per dispatch.** Write `<package>/drivers/<reviewer>.json` with `{"reviewer": "<name>", "slices": [<ids dispatched>], "result": "raw/<reviewer>.txt", "definition": "<path of the reviewer's SKILL.md>"}`: `ledger build` takes the reviewer's rule file from `definition` (a `skill_path` there, or inside a `payload` object, is read too) and the slices it was handed from `slices`. Only reviewer replies belong in `raw/`; a verification payload or a note filed there is reported as set aside and left in place, but it still costs a step. On `INCOMPLETE`, `BLOCKED` or `NEEDS_CONTEXT` (never accepted as a finished scope), and on a `DONE` that left slices open, `keryx review retry-plan --manifest <package>/slices/manifest.json --result <package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt --package <package>` decides and hands out the next wave of only the slices still uncovered (`--next-wave` plans one without a result). A result that covered a new slice spends no attempt; two results in a row with nothing new, or six failed rounds, print the `- **Not run:** …` line to paste into the report, and a result with nothing new first has its open slices cut in half. `keryx review slice --package <package>` already wrote one driver per reviewer x wave (`drivers/<reviewer>-w<n>.json`: slice ids, absolute slice paths, `result` path; the dispatcher adds `model`). Dispatch each wave in one batch, save each reply to its driver's `result`, and after each batch run `keryx review next --package <package>` (never `retry-plan` once per reviewer): it returns every reviewer's next wave at once, with reason `missing`, `retry`, `stalled` or `escalated`, or `done`. **While the plan is authorized, do not stop between batches.** The plan is authorized when `keryx review estimate` asks for no confirmation or the confirmation is recorded; `next` says so with the line "plan authorized; continue the loop without asking the operator; stop only for the card list, for plan growth, or on done / Not run" (`--json`: `planAuthorized`, `continue`). Then dispatch what it returned in the same turn: no "continue?", no "launch the next wave?", no "close with waivers or continue?", and no end of turn before `next` prints `done` or the reviewer is `Not run`. The stops are the closed list in `SKILL.detail.md` § "Between waves" and nothing else. After a crash or timeout run it first: it collects late results from `<package>/raw/` and never re-hands a finished slice. Only the operator can accept a smaller set than that (the `review_override_reviewers` card, or their answer to the host question recorded with `keryx review override-reviewers`, "Hosts"). An unfinished reviewer is never counted as a clean pass. **Persist every result, on every host.** On keryx shell pass each reviewer `save_result_to: <package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt`: the host writes its full final text there. Elsewhere the prompt tells the reviewer to write its whole reply to `<package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt` before it answers. Either way `review complete` has raw evidence after the transcript is cut, and you parse that file, never the tool output. Build `research.json` with `keryx review ledger build --package <package>` — never by hand: it reads the saved results, `scope-files.json` and the retry state, marks a reviewer complete only when its result is finished and its payloads cover the scope, and prints each gap with the exact next command and the waves left (a `retry-plan --next-wave` call, or a `--dispositions` entry for a raw finding). Run `keryx review ingest --research <package>/research.json` once it prints READY (exit 0). A refused `review_complete` card (or `keryx review complete` at a human's terminal) names what is missing: fix that with a command and close again; it is never `blocked`. `--head` wants a SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`), not `HEAD`.
 5. **Never print a scope or a slice.** The tool output of one call is cut at about 20 KB and `keryx review scope` of a large PR prints hundreds of KB. Run it as `keryx review scope --ref <base> --json > .metaproject/data/review/scope.json` and read the counts from the file (`keryx ctx read`, or `jq`); take `<base>` from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, not a guessed `origin/main`. Create `.metaproject/data/review/` first (`mkdir -p`) — a missing directory is a command to run, not a blocker. **Machine artifacts by direct write.** Save slices, payloads and results by redirection or `keryx ctx run --raw -- <command>`; the summarized form of `keryx ctx run` drops the bytes a later step parses.
 6. **Write mutants whole.** A testing reviewer's `mutant_candidates` cover every changed branch, code downstream of the diff included. Write them to `research-evidence/mutants.json` unchanged; you may not narrow them, and a candidate no pass has run still blocks the coverage gate (`SKILL.detail.md`, mutation pass).
 7. **Measure before `review-layout`.** Run the browser measurements (Playwright/Storybook) yourself and pass them in its first dispatch (`context_files` on keryx shell, by path elsewhere); they count as evidence when the command and viewport are named. A second `NEEDS_CONTEXT` from one role is Not run (`layout: no engine`), not another refill (`SKILL.detail.md`).
 
 ## Control
 
 - **Profiles.** The default is read-only: one round, no edits. `--fix` hands the findings to `flow-orchestrator` or `task-implementer`; the orchestrator never edits code. Control returns to this main session after each hand-off, which loads this skill again (never the implementer, which would nest); each re-review counts toward the ceiling (it adds 1 to the count).
 - **Waves.** Split by diff domain (`core` = logic, security, architecture; `domain` = frontend, backend, conventions; `support` = style, tests), in that order; A/B/C/D below keep their dependency order, except Wave C, which starts early and overlaps A and B (see Wave C); Wave D runs after the last verifier pass. A full or `--all` round runs at most 10 reviewers per wave (`MAX_REVIEWERS_PER_WAVE_FULL`).
 - **Rate limits.** On a reviewer dispatch that fails with a rate-limit or overloaded error (reported as `STATUS: RATE_LIMITED`, a harness signal, not a schema status), halve the wave, requeue the rest and honour `retry-after`, at most 300 seconds (`MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS`). After at most two halvings (`MAX_RATE_HALVINGS`) stop with `STATUS: BLOCKED rate_limited`, naming the queue left.
 - **Early verdict.** When every reviewer and the verifier are done, save every verifier pass to `research-evidence/verifications.json`, then run `keryx review verdict <package>` (it reads `<package>/raw`; the shared `.metaproject/data/review/raw` only when passed as `--raw`, which mixes in other rounds) and give the operator the verdict then; refuted findings are excluded only once `verifications.json` exists, held ones only once Wave D's claims are saved to `research-evidence/premises.json`. A verdict given before Wave D ran is provisional, and you say so: it counts as open the findings the judge may still hold or lower. The mutation pass, ledger and the `review_complete` card continue as the tail, and every managed round finishes them. The verdict is interim: the round is not done until `complete` (`SKILL.detail.md` § "Early verdict").

- `.metaproject/reviews/blast-radius.json` (or `.metaproject/flows/<flow>/reviews/blast-radius.json` for a flow-attached round) — the handoff slot, read when no flag is passed. The ingest **consumes** it: copied into the package it screened and removed from the slot, so a later round cannot be screened against a set nobody recomputed.
 
 Do **not** write the record inside the package directory before the ingest. A round that names no `--review-id` has not allocated that directory yet, and creating it makes the ingest take the next free name instead.
 
 `review-degradation` (profile `full`, deep tier) asks what the regression screen does not: is the code worse than on the base, and can that be shown? It reads the diff plus the importers of the module that holds each changed shared export (and of a barrel that re-exports it), which `keryx review blast-radius --degradation [--degradation-cap <n>]` prints from the code graph under one cap shared by all exports; the model never picks the set. It has no severity floor and needs no `--blast-radius` record. A `major` or `blocker` of its with no `evidence_kind` is lowered to `info` at ingest and listed in `scope.md` under `## Degradation evidence screen`. A light round does not dispatch it. A delta round dispatches it on a fix slice that changes a source-code file (not a test, a document or a data file) and on every new deep slice; a fix slice's lines cannot tell whether they sit inside an exported function, so the payload settles it.
 
 `--refuted` takes the findings this round **raised and then dismissed**, in the
 same finding shape, each carrying `disposition: {state, evidence}` with one of
 the `dismissed-*` states. Without it a package keeps only the survivors of an
 unlogged triage — which is why precision measured over the recorded corpus
 returns 100% whatever the reviewers actually got right.
 
 The `review_complete` card records what became of a finding when the fix round closes: pass `dispositions`, a list of `{finding, disposition, evidence}`, one per finding; the operator sees each on the card.
 At a human's terminal the same is `review complete --finding <id> --disposition <state> --evidence <ref>`, a triple repeatable per finding.
 States: `unknown`, `acted-on`, `dismissed-incorrect`,
 `dismissed-wont-fix`, `dismissed-out-of-scope`, `dismissed-deprioritised`.
 Everything except `unknown` must cite where the outcome is written down — the
 commit, the test, the decision. A recorded state and its citation cannot be
 overwritten by a later close; record a correction as a new round.
 
-`review complete` on a PR-bound package refuses a merged PR or a moved head unless `report.md`'s first line names the reviewed SHA and says so; a package with no PR binding is unaffected.
+`review complete` on a PR-bound package refuses a merged PR or a moved head unless the operator waives readiness item `head` (`review_waive_readiness` card, or `--waive head "<operator quote>"`); the report's first line still names the reviewed SHA for readers, but it unlocks nothing. A package with no PR binding is unaffected.
 `review complete` refuses a report with no `Evidence level:` line (`static only — did not run: <what>` or `ran — <what>`); a package ingested before the field existed only warns.
 `review ingest` keeps an internal finding whose `quote` is not at its `path` at the reviewed SHA (absent, or in several places) with no line, flagged `quote_unlocated`, instead of refusing the round (readiness item `quotes-located` lists it until it has a disposition); it still refuses, naming the finding, a quote it could not check at all (commit not in the checkout, no file named, or a size bound), and adds a `citation not found` line, never a deletion, to a rebuttal citing a rule or document that is not in the tree.
 A finding may close as `narrowed` (research obligation `"status":"narrowed","remains":"<what remains>"`); it counts as closed only with that text, and the report keeps it under "Refuted and narrowed".
 
 **Closing a fix round without dispositions leaves every finding reading `unknown`.** That is not "the reviewers were right"; it is "nobody wrote down what happened", and it is the single reason the precision figure cannot be read.
 
 Managed modes:
 
 - `lightweight`: report-only; no flow or managed review artifacts are created, and nothing is posted — no `comments reply`.
 - `attach-review`: write under
   `.metaproject/flows/<flow-dir>/reviews/<review-id>/`.
 - `review-flow`: write under `.metaproject/reviews/<review-id>/`.
 - `ingest`: convert an existing review report into managed findings, decisions,
   and learning handoff, attached to a flow when one is explicit or matched.
 
 Required artifacts for managed modes:
 
 - `manifest.json`
 - `scope.md`
 - `coverage.md`

| Machine `verdict` | First line |
 |---|---|
 | `REQUEST_CHANGES` | `**Changes requested — N Blocker, N Major, N Minor, N questions.**` |
 | `APPROVE` | `**No blockers, merge-ready.**` |
 | `APPROVE_WITH_SUGGESTIONS` | `**No blockers, merge-ready — N Minor, N questions.**` |
 
 `N` counts findings **in the changed code** at that severity. A
 `location_class: pre-existing` finding is not counted and does not flip the
 verdict. Omit a zero count. A question is an `info` finding that needs an
 author answer, rendered under Questions, not as a finding.
 
 The second line is the context line: head, base, round, size, CI. If head moved
 during the round, add `· unchecked: <commits>`.
 
 The third line is the **evidence level** and is required: `Evidence level: static
 only — did not run: <what>` when nothing was executed, or `Evidence level: ran —
 <what ran>`. `keryx review complete` refuses a report without it.
 
 When the PR was merged or its head moved after the review, the report's first line
-says so and names the reviewed SHA, or `keryx review complete` refuses.
+says so and names the reviewed SHA. That line informs the reader only:
+`keryx review complete` still refuses until the operator waives readiness item `head`.
 
 ### Refuted and narrowed
 
 One line per finding that did not stand as reported, kept with its evidence so a
 reader sees what was claimed and why it was set aside:
 
 ```markdown
 - **F-007. Dismissed** — <the author's rebuttal, quoted>. <citation not found: …> where the cited rule is not in the tree.
 - **F-009. Narrowed** — <what the finding claimed>. **Remains:** <what is still open>. Evidence: <what was run>.
 ```
 
 A narrowed finding counts as closed only with its "Remains" text.

+# Процесс ревью в keryx: архитектура, функциональность, продукт
+
+Срез: `origin/main` на `66ee00117` (v0.4.26), 2026-11-12. Только чтение: тесты не запускались, код не менялся.
+
+Пометки у находок: **[проверено]** — я сам прочитал код или файл, который это доказывает; **[со слов аудита]** — получено от одного из четырёх параллельных аудитов и мной не перепроверено.
+
+## Вердикт
+
+Идеи в основе процесса сильные и редкие: верификатор, который может только удалять и обязан что-то запустить; судья предпосылок; привязка находки к цитате, а не к номеру строки; запись каждого решения оператора. Но вокруг этих идей выросла система, которая не выполняет трёх собственных обещаний.
+
+1. **Гейты закрытия на хостах без карточек держатся на честности агента.** Три из них снимаются текстом, который пишет сам агент.
+2. **Стоимость и длительность раунда никто не знает**, а выбор модели для ревьюеров на keryx shell молча не работает.
+3. **Раунд не сходится и почти никогда не закрывается**: 2 закрытых пакета из 36, в среднем 3 раунда на PR, 79% находок — minor и info.
+
+Главный архитектурный диагноз: у раунда нет модели состояния в коде. Порядок шагов живёт в 233 КБ прозы оркестратора, а код — это 58 независимых подкоманд, каждая из которых заново выводит состояние из файлов пакета. Поэтому каждая новая проблема лечится новым абзацем в скиле и новым гейтом в CLI, а не изменением автомата.
+
+## Как раунд устроен на самом деле
+
+Раунд — это каталог `.metaproject/reviews/<id>/`. Каждая стадия — отдельный глагол CLI из одной цепочки `if` в `src/commands/review.ts:739-1000`. Диспетчеризацию ревьюеров делает агент-хост, а не keryx: keryx пишет драйверы, читает ответы из `raw/*.txt` и считает, что ещё не покрыто.
+
+Стадии: `start` (пакет, `round.json`) → `scope`, `blast-radius`, `slice`, `required`, `estimate` → волны A/B (ревьюеры), C (верификатор), D (судья предпосылок) → `ledger build` → `ingest` → `verdict` → `readiness` (12 пунктов) → `complete` → `publish`.
+
+Объём: `src/review` — 161 модуль без тестов, 52,5 тыс. строк, плюс 168 файлов тестов. `src/commands/review.ts` — 5 940 строк. Оркестратор — `SKILL.md` 147 КБ и `SKILL.detail.md` 86 КБ.
+
+## Критичные находки
+
+### 1. Три гейта закрытия снимаются текстом агента [проверено]
+
+- **Гейт верификатора.** `verifierCheck` пропускает неверифицированные blocker и major, если в `report.md` есть строка `Not verified: N` (`src/review/readiness.ts:228-235`). Отчёт пишет агент, а сообщение об отказе само подсказывает, какую строку добавить.
+- **Гейт сдвинутой головы PR.** Проходит, если первая строка отчёта называет SHA и содержит слово о том, что PR сдвинулся (`src/review/complete-head-gate.ts:56-58`).
+- **Перезапись проверенного коммита.** `--head <sha>` заменяет записанную при старте голову, оставляя только предупреждение (`src/review/managed.ts:1043-1055`). Если передать текущую голову PR, проверка сдвига становится ложной.
+- **Ответ оператора через вопрос хоста.** На Claude Code, Codex и прочих `--answered-by` принимает источник и текст ответа со слов модели. Блокировка есть только по переменным окружения keryx (`src/review/managed.ts:1059`), которых эти хосты не ставят.
+
+Почему важно: вся ценность записи «оператор решил» в том, что агент не может её подделать. На keryx shell карточки это обеспечивают, на остальных хостах — нет.
+
+Направление: приравнять текстовые аттестации в отчёте к вейверам с тем же доказательством (карточка или TTY); `--head` принимать только для коммита, который является предком записанного; в опубликованном теле помечать решения, принятые через вопрос хоста, как непроверенные.
+
+### 2. Вейвер одного пункта обнуляет все ошибки research-гейта [проверено]
+
+`src/review/managed.ts:1105-1107`: вейвер любого из `files-covered`, `blast-radius`, `reviewers`, `ledger` делает `researchProblems = []` целиком. Оператор снимает один пункт, а пропускаются все.
+
+Направление: фильтровать ошибки по тому пункту, который снят.
+
+### 3. Публикация не стоит после закрытия [проверено]
+
+`publishReview` (`src/review/publish.ts:146-180`) не смотрит на `manifest.status` и не берёт блокировку закрытия. Готовность она пересчитывает сама, но проверки подмены `round.json` и уровня доказательности (`managed.ts:1039`, `1075-1082`) есть только на пути `complete`. В GitHub может уйти ревью из пакета, который `complete` отказался бы закрыть.
+
+Направление: одна функция `evaluateGates(package, action)`, которую вызывают `complete`, `publish`, `status` и стоп-гейт сессии. Сейчас стоп-гейт проверяет строгое подмножество того, на чём отказывает `complete` (`managed.ts:922-932`) [со слов аудита].
+
+### 4. Выбор модели для ревьюеров на keryx shell не работает [проверено]
+
+Оркестратор велит передавать `model_tier: light|standard|deep` (`SKILL.md:118`). `spawn_subagent` это поле игнорирует и пишет уведомление о миграции (`src/harness/tool/builtin/spawn-subagent-tool.ts:1497-1498`). Рабочее поле — `model_class` со значениями `light|standard|expert|frontier`; в ревью-скилах оно не упоминается ни разу, а значения `deep` в нём нет.
+
+Следствие: `keryx review tier` и оценка стоимости плана описывают не то, что реально запускалось.
+
+Направление: перевести скил на `model_class` и добавить контрактный тест, который падает, когда скил называет поле спавна, игнорируемое схемой.
+
+### 5. «Кросс-семейная верификация» не исполняется [проверено частично]
+
+`keryx providers cross-family` никогда не запускает ревью, а только решает, допустимо ли оно, и печатает запись (`src/standard/command-registry.ts:1742-1743`, проверено). Что `checkCrossFamilyReview` проверяет лишь внутреннюю согласованность записи — со слов аудита. Раунд может нести `mode=cross-family`, хотя ни один ревьюер на другом семействе не работал.
+
+Направление: либо добавить шаг диспетчеризации и связать его `executionId` с записью, либо переименовать поле в «допустимость», чтобы отчёт не намекал на второе мнение.
+
+### 6. Стоимость и время раунда неизвестны [со слов аудита]
+
+Во всех современных пакетах `research.json` показывает usage `known=0`; время раунда не пишется нигде. Единственная цифра — от 2026-09-15: 552 тыс. токенов на раунд, 92 тыс. на сохранённую находку. При 22–26 диспатчах на раунд это главный вопрос пользователя, и на него нет ответа. На хостах без keryx shell учёт токенов вообще ручной: оркестратор должен сам дописать строку `KERYX_USAGE` (`SKILL.md:45`, проверено).
+
+Направление: сделать захват usage пунктом готовности либо убрать обещания о стоимости; первой строкой отчёта печатать время и токены.
+
+## Архитектура
+
+**Нет автомата раунда.** В перечислении статусов пять значений, а пишутся только `draft` и `closed`; `round-record.ts` ветвится по `reviewed|decided|learned`, которые никто не записывает [со слов аудита]. Состояние раунда — объединение файлов, выводимое заново при каждом вызове.
+
+**Правила продублированы в прозе и в коде.** Правило «нужен ли раунд» записано абзацем в `SKILL.md:29` и функцией `classifyRoundNeed`; сам скил признаёт, что CLI функцию не вызывает. Я проверил: у неё нет ни одного вызова вне тестов. Агент исполняет прозу, тест следит, чтобы проза и код не разошлись. Это должна быть команда.
+
+**Потолок длины скила измеряется в строках и только опускается** (`src/gdskills/skill-length-ceilings.ts`) [проверено]. Оркестратор стоит ровно на потолке в 1 571 строку, а растёт внутрь строк: 5 строк длиннее 1 500 символов, самая длинная — 5 023 символа (`SKILL.md:128`, один абзац про волны). Вторая отдушина — `SKILL.detail.md` без потолка. Метрика достигла обратного: текст стал плотнее и менее читаемым для модели.
+
+**Высокая текучесть.** 93 коммита в `SKILL.md` оркестратора за 60 дней [проверено]; 20% пунктов changelog за 30 релизов касаются ревью [со слов аудита]. В операционном промпте остаётся история: «одиннадцать раундов во flow 127 и 128», «исправлено с 0.2.70», цифры из arXiv. Это оплачивается токенами в каждом раунде и принадлежит ADR.
+
+**Бог-файлы и плоское пространство имён** [со слов аудита, размер `review.ts` проверен]. `review.ts` — 5 940 строк, `managed.ts` — 3 187 строк и 104 функции (создание пакета, ingest, устаревший парсер прозы, диспозиции, закрытие, рендер). Имена вводят в заблуждение: `completion-gate.ts` — это стоп-гейт сессии, а не гейт закрытия; `floor.ts` и `arbiter-floor.ts` — несвязанные понятия. Восемь `jev-*-config.ts` — один и тот же 25-строчный читатель с разным ключом.
+
+**Четыре несвязанные абстракции «хоста»** [со слов аудита]: `host-profile.ts` (перечисление из четырёх значений, управляет только размером волны), `completion-host.ts` (происхождение ответа оператора), иерархический движок `review/agents` (настоящий порт с флагами возможностей, только keryx shell, включается `--hierarchical`) и файловая сторона плоского пути. Первая и третья никак не соединены.
+
+**Конкурентность** [со слов аудита]: блокировку берут только закрытие и вейверы; `ingest` и `ledger build` пишут `findings.json` и `research.json` без неё. Снимок содержимого при закрытии не включает `verifications.json`, записи мутаций и `round.json`, которые читает готовность.
+
+**Сквозного теста нет** [со слов аудита, выведено из выборки]: тесты закрытия подают собранный вручную ledger, а не тот, что построил `ledger build`. Цепочку start → slice → ledger → ingest → complete → publish не гоняет ни один тест.
+
+## Функциональность: скилы и субагенты
+
+**Канонический рубрикатор серьёзности противоречит скилам, которые на него ссылаются** [проверено]. Оркестратор задаёт blocker как «ровно четыре формы». При этом `review-highload` ставит blocker по пунктам чек-листа 11 раз (например, строки 126, 283, 353), `review-backend` — 7 раз (строки 87–162). Это прямой источник завышенной серьёзности.
+
+**Скил учит тому, что запрещает схема** [проверено]. Отрицательное перечисление: `class_scope.sites: []` в `SKILL.md:1361`, а в `reviewer-finding.schema.json:158` у `sites` стоит `minItems: 1`. Как на это реагирует ingest, не проверялось.
+
+**Два конкурирующих шаблона находки** [со слов аудита]. Схема требует `impact`, `suggested_fix`, `evidence`, `confidence`; встроенные markdown-шаблоны в 18 скилах дают «Why it matters» и «Fix» без evidence и confidence.
+
+**Ревьюерам велят делать то, чего они не могут** [со слов аудита]. Скилы говорят «команд не запускаю», а в чек-листах остались «определи git-scope» и «собери diff». `review-layout` и `review-ui-ux` требуют измерений в браузере и dev-сервера при заявленном read-only.
+
+**Стековые допущения утекают в чужие проекты.** `stack_requires: "react,mobx"` срабатывает при любом из тегов (`SKILL.md:861`, проверено), так что React-проект без MobX получает всю MobX-ветку. Без всякого гейта остаются NestJS в `review-architecture` и `review-security-code`, префикс `I` для интерфейсов в `review-style`, жёстко зашитый `src/core/**` [со слов аудита].
+
+**Пересечения гарантируют дубликаты** [со слов аудита]: N+1 и индексы — в performance, highload и backend; naming и DRY — в style и clean-code. В прогоне PR 1058 из 109 сырых находок осталось 16 канонических, одну нашли независимо 11 ревьюеров.
+
+**Измерения без владельца** [со слов аудита]: зависимости и лицензии, совместимость публичного API, наблюдаемость, обработка ошибок, i18n.
+
+**Jev-скилы — это программы, а не ревьюеры** [со слов аудита]: они несут `model_tier`, триггеры и «общие законы» для LLM, ссылаются на внутренние номера flow и уезжают в чужие проекты, где без ключа инертны. По собственным замерам проекта они проигрывают сильной модели (recall рисков 21% против 44%) и выключены по умолчанию.
+
+**Пара «только удаление» спроектирована верно**, но с тремя дырами [со слов аудита]: слияние не проверяет, что `execution`-доказательство — действительно вывод команды (достаточно непустой строки); `site-check` может опровергнуть находку из-за того, что поиск пропускает скрытые каталоги; судья может временно убрать blocker из открытых, сославшись на гайдлайн, который никто не сверяет.

+## Харнесы
+
+Плоский путь с параллельными субагентами работает на keryx shell и Claude Code. Остальное — со слов аудита, кроме помеченного.
+
+- **Codex, opencode, Grok** не имеют инструмента спавна и уходят в `keryx review run --autonomous` (`SKILL.md:28`, проверено). Этот раннер поднимает вложенный `keryx shell` на провайдере keryx. Пользователь, выбравший Codex или Grok, получает ревью другой моделью и должен отдельно настроить ключи keryx.
+- **opencode и Grok** нигде не первоклассны: в перечислении хостов их нет, определяются как `other`; экспорта скилов для Grok нет.
+- **Claude Code**: нет карточек, поэтому закрытие и публикация — только в терминале оператора, а четыре акта идут через непроверяемый вопрос хоста. В прогоне PR 1124 все ревьюеры шли через `general-purpose`, то есть именованные агенты не использовались.
+- **CI-бот**: один проход ревьюера плюс верификатор, один провайдер, workflow существует только как пример в `docs/examples`; гайд признаёт, что против настоящего GitHub он не запускался.
+- **Три режима лимитов на одно ревью**: дедлайн ребёнка 5 минут на shell, собственные потолки иерархического движка (12 и 32), размер волны в байтах по хосту (60 000 против 150 000).

+## Что сделано хорошо
+
+- **Слияние верификатора — только удаление, по построению**: в схеме нет полей серьёзности и текста проблемы, в коде нет пути эскалации, каждое отклонение записывается с причиной.
+- **Закрытие транзакционно**: блокировка, снимок содержимого, сравнение перед каждым переименованием, откат только своих записей.
+- **Защита входов раунда от подмены**: `round.json` и `prior_findings.json` хэшируются в манифесте, а реестр завершённых раундов лежит вне репозитория, так что PR не может подделать прошлый раунд.
+- **Привязка по цитате вместо номера строки** — исправление измеренной проблемы (18,6% находок указывали на файл, которого не было на записанной голове).
+- **Честное самоизмерение**: документы прямо говорят, что Jev проигрывает сильной модели, что бот не запускался вживую, что точность по корпусу читать нельзя.
+- **Тесты на реальных путях**: временные каталоги, настоящий git и настоящая команда, а не моки.

 Review V3 uses one foreground owner process for ordinary terminals and external harnesses. `serve` prints an explicit
 Unix-socket handshake containing `KERYX_REVIEW_AGENTS_ROOT_SOCKET`, `KERYX_REVIEW_AGENTS_ROOT_TOKEN`, and
 `KERYX_REVIEW_AGENTS_ROOT_RUNS_ROOT`; export all three only into the controlling Codex CLI, Claude Code, or other harness.
 The bearer grants the fixed host ceiling selected at `serve` startup, so do not persist it in configuration, logs, or
 child-agent environments. Root commands fail closed on a partial environment. Descendant agents receive a different,
 run-scoped bridge grant and cannot combine it with the root environment.
 
 The operator-only steps here (`confirm-plan`, `waive-mutation`, `override-reviewers`, `decide-premise`, `chunks estimate --answer`, `complete --waive-coverage`, `complete --waive`, `publish`) need a terminal, except that the first four also accept a host question (below); plain `complete` has no terminal check, so for an agent the card rule below is what binds it (TM-04 section 8). Inside `keryx shell` the agent calls `review_confirm_plan`, `review_decide_premise`, `review_chunks_answer`, `review_complete`, `review_waive_coverage`, `review_waive_readiness` or `review_publish` instead and never sends the operator to a terminal for them: the operator answers a card in the shell or, when remote control is on, in the Telegram topic, and the record carries `confirmedVia: tui-card` or `remote-card` (the latter with `pressedBy` and `pressedAt`). A remote answer is accepted only from an allowed Telegram user id, for this card, once, within one hour; without a reachable topic the card says "Telegram mirror not delivered" and is answered in the shell. `/remote-control` and `/decisions` list the cards waiting and answered. The two waiver tools only record the waiver; the agent then closes the review through the `review_complete` card, never by running `keryx review complete`, which stays for a human in a terminal (TM-04). An autonomous (unattended) run is excluded from this card gate: it is not given the card tools and closes the package through `keryx review complete` as before.
 
 **A host question.** Outside keryx shell there is no card tool. For four acts the agent asks the operator with the host's own question tool (Claude Code's question tool, Codex's, a Telegram poll through Helyx), offering the verb's options (`yes` or `no` for `confirm-plan`, `waive` or `keep`, `override` or `keep`, `uphold` or `dismiss`) and naming the subject in the question (the plan numbers, the mutant ids or their count, the reviewer names, the finding id), and records the answer with `confirm-plan`, `waive-mutation`, `override-reviewers` or `decide-premise` and, with no terminal, `--answered-by <source>:<ref> --answer-text "<the operator's words, verbatim>" --question-text "<the question as asked>"`. `<source>` is `claude-code` or `codex` for the host harness's own question tool (`<ref>` its question id), `helyx-poll` for a Telegram poll (`<ref>` is `<poll-id>[:<message-id>]`), `keryx-shell` only for a plain question the shell itself asked (in keryx shell use the card first) or `other` (`<ref>` a message id or a short label). `decide-premise` still takes `--answer uphold|dismiss --reason "<why>"`; the other two still take `--reason`. `confirm-plan` refuses a stale plan: `--question-text` must show the plan's current dispatch count and minute range (as `keryx review estimate` prints them), otherwise ask the operator again with the current numbers. The record carries `confirmedVia: "host-question"` with the source, ref, question and answer, and a `keryx decisions` entry is written; the review report and `/decisions` show it apart from a card. keryx does not verify the answer: a host question is weaker than a card press (`tui-card`, `remote-card`), which stays the first choice where a card is available (TM-04 section 6b, [limitations](limitations.md)). Nothing is recorded, and the command exits non-zero, for an answer that is not one of the verb's options (free text is not a decision), a decline (words or `--answer`), `decide-premise` words that name the other choice or none, an empty answer or question, a malformed `--answered-by`, an unknown package, a finding that is not held, a stale plan or a missing `--reason`. +### Gates that keep a report honest
 
-- **The PR moved.** `keryx review complete` on a PR-bound package asks the tracker for the PR. When it is merged or its head is no longer the reviewed SHA, completion is refused until the first line of `report.md` names the reviewed SHA and says so ("Reviewed `1a2b3c4` — the PR has since merged."). A package is PR-bound when it targets a pull request or when its `--ref` is a pull request URL, even if it was ingested with `--target report`; a package with no PR binding is not asked; a tracker that cannot be reached is a warning, not a refusal.
-- **Evidence level.** A report carries one line, `Evidence level: static only — did not run: <what>` or `Evidence level: ran — <what ran>`, and `complete` refuses a report without it. A package ingested before the field existed completes with a warning.
+- **The PR moved.** `keryx review complete` on a PR-bound package asks the tracker for the PR. When it is merged or its head is no longer the reviewed SHA, readiness item `head` fails and completion is refused. Nothing the agent writes into `report.md` lifts it: you waive `head` in your own words (`--waive head "<your words>"`, or the `review_waive_readiness` card), and the report then opens with a `Partial review:` line. `keryx review publish` fails the same item. A package is PR-bound when it targets a pull request or when its `--ref` is a pull request URL, even if it was ingested with `--target report`; a package with no PR binding is not asked; a tracker that cannot be reached is a warning, not a refusal.
+- **Evidence level.** A report carries one line, `Evidence level: static only — did not run: <what>` or `Evidence level: ran — <what ran>`, and `complete` and `publish` refuse a report without it (`publish --partial` does not relax this, nor the round-record check below). A package ingested before the field existed completes with a warning.
+- **Round record.** `complete` and `publish` run one shared gate evaluation: a round record (`round.json`, `prior_findings.json`) edited after `review start` is refused by both, with the same message.
+- **Relabelled head.** `review complete --head <sha>` names the commit the round ran against. When it differs from the head `review start` recorded, it needs your own words (`--head-reason "<your words>"`, at a terminal or with `--answered-by` from a host question): the refusal names both SHAs, and the manifest records `head_override` with the previous head, the new head and your words. A `--head` equal to the recorded head needs nothing.
+- **Host questions.** A decision the agent recorded from its host's own question (`confirmedVia: host-question`) is reported provenance, not an attestation. The posted review says which decisions came that way and that keryx did not verify the operator's answer.
+- **A waiver covers its own item.** Waiving `files-covered`, `blast-radius`, `reviewers` or `ledger` removes only the research errors that belong to that item; an artifact-locator or manifest/dispatch mismatch error still refuses the close.
 - **Citations.** When a dismissal's rebuttal cites a rule or document, `review ingest` looks the path up in the tree (at the reviewed commit and as it stands) and, if it is not there, adds a `citation not found: <path>` line to the finding's evidence. The finding is never deleted.
 - **Narrowed.** A research obligation may close as `narrowed` with a `remains` text ("what is still open"). It counts as closed only with that text, and the report keeps it under "Refuted and narrowed" with its evidence.
 - **Locators at the SHA.** `review ingest` reads each finding's quote at its `path` at the reviewed SHA, not from the working tree. A quote absent from that file, or in it more than once, does not refuse the round (flow 460): the finding is kept with no line, never relocated by similarity, flagged `quote_unlocated` (with the candidate lines when ambiguous), listed in scope.md, and readiness item `quotes-located` fails until it has a disposition or the operator waives it. The ingest still refuses, naming the finding, a quote it could not check at all: the commit is not in the checkout, no file is named, or a size bound stopped the match. The report links the blob at that SHA.
 
 ### The one dismissal that teaches something
 
 `dismissed-incorrect` — and only that state — writes a note into
 `.metaproject/memory/review-notes/`, naming the finding, the reviewer, why it was
 dismissed, and the round and commit it came from:
 
 ```console
 $ keryx review complete <path> --finding F-002 --disposition dismissed-incorrect \
     --evidence "human: alice ran the writer under umask 002; the mode is 0700"
 review-note: 2026-08-03-round6#F-002 -> .metaproject/memory/review-notes/2026-08-03-round6__F-002.md (attested by human)
 ```
 
 The other three dismissals write nothing, deliberately. They say the finding was
 *correct* and not worth doing now; feeding them into a learning signal teaches
 the reviewer to stop raising true findings, and in the resulting `SKILL.md` that
 is indistinguishable from having learned something real.
